question: On 1 February 2024, a large number of factory workers at Hutchinson Borrachas de Portugal Lda, Campo Maior, went on strike.

With this strike – the first since this automotive component factory was established in 1999 – the workers reiterated their list of demands for 2024: a fair and dignified increase in their wages, a greater meal allowance, seniority payments, overtime rates for work carried out on Saturdays and on public holidays and an additional day off for workers on their birthday.

This factory belongs to the Hutchinson Group, a multinational corporation that has a presence in more than 25 countries, that generated a revenue of EUR 4.4 billion in 2022 and that forms an integral part of the large multinational corporation Total Energies. In light of this: 1.
Has the Hutchinson Group, or any of its subsidiaries, ever received – or is it currently receiving – any kind of European funding?
Does the Commission know if other European factories are facing similar situations? Are workers in any of the group’s other factories protesting?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.4.2024) 1. The Hutchinson group is present in eight other Member States.

The three companies of the Hutchinson group in Portugal were granted a total of EUR 5,467,772 in support from European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and EUR 62,055 from European Social Fund (ESF) for 4 projects during the 2014-2020 programming period, through the COMPETE operational programme under the thematic objectives ‘research and innovation processes in large companies’ and ‘adaptation of workers, companies and entrepreneurs to change’.

In addition, during the same period, the Hutchinson group has received funding through the ERDF in three projects in Poland, with EU co-financing of PLN 8,173,326, and in one project in Czechia, with EU co-financing of CZK 6,940,777. 2. On 12 December 2023, around 100 employees of Hutchinson were on strike in ChateauGontier-sur-Mayenne, in France, demanding a salary increase to compensate inflation.
In June 2022, the workers of the group's factory in Żywiec, in Poland, protested for a week. This strike ended with an agreement to increase wages.

While the right to strike falls under the responsibility of each Member State1, the Commission stresses the importance of a meaningful social dialogue and of the promotion of fair working conditions as essential aspects of the European Pillar of Social Rights2 and its action Plan3 – notably principle 8 ‘social dialogue and involvement of workers’.

1 Article 153(5) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/social/main.jsp?catId=1226&langId=en 3 https://op.europa.eu/webpub/empl/european-pillar-of-social-rights/en
